(slime; also 1 other layout(s) in tracks/fly/layouts)

Payload family: the 6-block engine fly-horizontal-6b-10gt-e2cf52 carrying n blocks, 10 gt/block for every n: a column up from the front slime (slime, each drags the next; the top block gold), 9 at most (a piston moves at most 12 blocks: the 3-block part + 9), then a column down from the rear slime; n = 18 is the most the engine moves (a 10th block on the rear: the pull fails). (slime, carries 1 block(s))

flies horizontally at 9 gt/block, the fastest horizontal machine: the 6-block engine e2cf52 without its rear observer; a redstone block rides on the front part (on a second slime) beside the cell the rear piston lands in, so the pulled piston fires as it lands (1 gt) instead of waiting for an observer (2 gt); the front observer (riding, fires 2 gt after landing) drives the sticky puller (slime; also 1 other layout(s) in tracks/fly/layouts)

flies up at 9 gt/block in 6 blocks: a redstone block on the honey part fires the pusher as it lands (no rear observer); the front observer drives the sticky puller (slime + honey; also 3 other layout(s) in tracks/fly/layouts)

Train family: the 6-block engine fly-horizontal-6b-10gt-e2cf52 pulling n trailers, 10 gt/block for every n. A sticky piston on the rear slime (facing back, fired with the pusher by the rear observer) reach-pulls trailer 1 each cycle; every trailer but the last carries a sticky piston facing back and a rider observer (it fires into the trailer's slime 2 gt after the trailer lands) that pulls the next trailer, which starts against that piston's face. Each trailer is a piston move of its own (12 blocks at most), so the machine has no size limit: 5 + 3n blocks (a two-part machine moves at most 24). (slime, pulls 1 trailer(s))
